data.title: RXO (RXO) Stock Rebounds As Margin Relief Meets Cash Burn Doubts
data.description:
RXO stock jumped about 7% to US$21.70 after the Q2 print, a sharp move for a freight brokerage that has frustrated investors over the past month with a roughly 19% slide. The reaction hinges on one thing: the margin story finally showed some relief, even as the company remained loss making.

Adjusted earnings before interest, tax, depreciation and amortization came in at US$40 million and net income loss narrowed to US$9 million on US$1.8b of revenue. For a capital tight, cash hungry model, this earnings run rate matters far more than a single quarter’s headline loss per share.

  • Revenue, Q2 2026 vs. Q2 2025: US$1,774 million vs. US$1,419 million (up about 25%)
  • Net Income/Loss, Q2 2026 vs. Q2 2025: loss of US$9 million vs. loss of US$9 million (broadly flat year on year)
  • Basic EPS, Q2 2026 vs. Q2 2025: loss of US$0.05 per share vs. loss of US$0.05 per share (little change year on year)
  • Adjusted EBITDA, Q2 2026 vs. Q2 2025: US$40 million compared with a guidance range midpoint below this level (delivered above the guided high end for the quarter)

Evaluating RXO’s AI and Mix-Shift Bull Case

Bulls argue RXO can compound margins through AI driven productivity and a richer mix of less than truckload freight and last mile work. Q2 gives some concrete milestones. Brokerage revenue of about US$1.3b with truckload volume growth and higher gross profit per load shows the platform is converting tighter capacity and higher spot exposure into better yield, not just more loads. Management highlighted that its Agentic AI tools lifted spot quote activity and supported a double digit sequential gain in truckload profit per load, which aligns directly with the productivity part of the thesis.

The mix shift claim also shows some traction. Complementary Services revenue reached US$488 million with last mile revenue up and stops higher by 3%. That points to growing exposure to the higher margin, stickier segments bulls focus on, even though RXO is not yet back to broad based profitability.

RXO bear case on leverage, cash and liability

The bearish argument on RXO centers on three linked worries: high leverage with thin margins, a cash-hungry model that could force equity issuance, and rising legal and regulatory liability for freight brokers. Q2 does not fully clear these hurdles. Net leverage of 4.1x LTM bank-adjusted EBITDA remains elevated, and adjusted free cash flow was a US$42 million outflow as working capital and QuickPay usage absorbed cash. That keeps the short cash runway and dilution concern alive, even with US$350 million of liquidity and a US$200 million accordion.

On liability, the Supreme Court ruling that opened the door to more negligent hiring claims still hangs over the group. Management points to strong carrier vetting and insurance, yet renewals land in late December. Yet prior to the latest earnings, the analysts had been anticipated revenues of R$3.98b and earnings per share (EPS) of R$1.95 in 2026. So we can see that while the consensus made no real change to its revenue estimates, it also no longer provides an earnings per share estimate.
